ticket.title: reserve-namespaces.sh omits three workspace members, and the one name still free on crates.io is one of them
ticket.description:
MEASURED 2026-11-12, while deciding whether to hand this script to outfeed reserve (AF-22, now parked on GB-362).

THE DRIFT
The script hand-maintains a CRATES array of 10 names. The workspace has 12 members plus an umbrella
name that only exists to hold the namespace, so the set that needs holding is 13.

  workspace members (12, from Cargo.toml members + each member's [package] name)
    aerofoil-1090 aerofoil-978 aerofoil-cli aerofoil-common aerofoil-mcp aerofoil-mlat
    aerofoil-persistence aerofoil-replay aerofoil-sdr aerofoil-server aerofoil-tracker aerofoil-tui

  script array (10)
    aerofoil (umbrella) aerofoil-common aerofoil-1090 aerofoil-978 aerofoil-tracker
    aerofoil-server aerofoil-cli aerofoil-mcp aerofoil-sdr aerofoil-persistence

  in the workspace, absent from the script
    aerofoil-mlat  aerofoil-replay  aerofoil-tui

WHICH OF THE THREE ACTUALLY MATTERS
Checking the registry directly (404 = free, 200 = taken):

  aerofoil-tui       TAKEN  0.1.0-beta.1, created 2026-11-10, description is ours
  aerofoil-replay    TAKEN  0.1.0-beta.1, created 2026-11-10, description is ours
  aerofoil-mlat      FREE   (404)

So two of the three are already ours and need no reservation - they were published from this workspace
on the 0.1.0-beta.1 release date, not reserved as placeholders. The third is the live hole:
aerofoil-mlat is unclaimed, and no artifact in this repository records that.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN A COUNT
`bash scripts/reserve-namespaces.sh check` answers "0 free, 10 taken" - a clean bill of health that is
silent about the only name a third party can still take. A published version can be yanked but never
deleted, so if someone claims aerofoil-mlat the workspace member at crates/mlat can never publish
under its own name; it would ship under a different one or not at all.

The hand-maintained array is how the drift happened: the list was correct when written (AF-20 reserved
eight names) and stopped being correct as members were added, with nothing to fail when that occurred.
Cargo.toml already couples the two files - `exclude = ["reserve-staging"]` exists precisely because
the staging tree lives inside the workspace - so deriving the names from the members is the natural
fix rather than a new mechanism.

NOT IN SCOPE
Converting the script to a wrapper around `outfeed reserve`: that is AF-22, parked on GB-362 because
no released outfeed carries the verb. This ticket is only about the list being true.
acceptance_criteria: reserve-namespaces.sh covers every workspace member plus the aerofoil umbrella name (13 today)
check names aerofoil-mlat as free until it is reserved, and reports the true count
the name list is derived from the workspace manifests, or a gate fails when a member is missing from it
after reservation the script's list and the registry agree, with every name TAKEN
